\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{मेषः} (meṣaḥ)}{मेषः (meṣaḥ)}]{\sk{मेषः} (meṣaḥ) — a sheep}

\label{lesson:SA-C114-mesah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a bull, then the Sanskrit for a buffalo.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{मेषः}}
\textbf{\sk{मेषः}} — \emph{meṣaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a sheep\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{meṣa} \textquotedblleft{}a ram, a sheep\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Indo-European (EtymDB): Avestan \emph{maēša} and Persian \emph{mīš} \textquotedblleft{}ewe\textquotedblright{} are cousins. In astronomy it names Aries, the first sign of the zodiac (MW). Hindi kept it as \emph{mes} \textquotedblleft{}ram\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10334).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{meṣaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{meṣaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{meṣaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a bull, then the Sanskrit for a buffalo, then say \emph{meṣaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{कपोतः} (kapotaḥ)}{कपोतः (kapotaḥ)}]{\sk{कपोतः} (kapotaḥ) — a pigeon}

\label{lesson:SA-C114-kapotah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a buffalo, then the Sanskrit for a sheep.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कपोतः}}
\textbf{\sk{कपोतः}} — \emph{kapotaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a pigeon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kapota} \textquotedblleft{}a dove, a pigeon\textquotedblright{} is old, in the Rigveda, and is inherited from Indo-Iranian (EtymDB). Its cousin is Persian \emph{kabūtar} \textquotedblleft{}pigeon\textquotedblright{}, which Hindi and Urdu took from Persian, so the Hindi pigeon is a Persian cousin of this Sanskrit word.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{उलूकः} (ulūkaḥ)}{उलूकः (ulūkaḥ)}]{\sk{उलूकः} (ulūkaḥ) — an owl}

\label{lesson:SA-C114-ulukah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a sheep, then the Sanskrit for a pigeon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{उलूकः}}
\textbf{\sk{उलूकः}} — \emph{ulūkaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}an owl\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ulūka} \textquotedblleft{}an owl\textquotedblright{} is old, in the Rigveda; MW cites only a grammarians' root √val for it, so its origin is uncertain. It lives on as Hindi \emph{ullū} \textquotedblleft{}owl\textquotedblright{}, and Punjabi and Gujarati \emph{ullū} also means \textquotedblleft{}fool\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2359).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{बकः} (bakaḥ)}{बकः (bakaḥ)}]{\sk{बकः} (bakaḥ) — a heron}

\label{lesson:SA-C114-bakah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a pigeon, then the Sanskrit for an owl.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{बकः}}
\textbf{\sk{बकः}} — \emph{bakaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a heron\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{baka} \textquotedblleft{}a heron, a crane\textquotedblright{} is probably imitative in origin, as CDIAL 9115 explains after EWA, which is why its \emph{k} survives into the modern forms. It lives on as Hindi \emph{bagulā} and Bengali \emph{bak} (CDIAL 9115).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{भ्रमरः} (bhramaraḥ)}{भ्रमरः (bhramaraḥ)}]{\sk{भ्रमरः} (bhramaraḥ) — a bee}

\label{lesson:SA-C114-bhramarah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for an owl, then the Sanskrit for a heron.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{भ्रमरः}}
\textbf{\sk{भ्रमरः}} — \emph{bhramaraḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a bee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bhramara} \textquotedblleft{}a large black bee\textquotedblright{} is filed by MW under the root √bhram \textquotedblleft{}wander, whirl\textquotedblright{}, which MW compares with Greek \emph{bremō} and Latin \emph{fremere} \textquotedblleft{}roar, hum\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB gives an Indo-European root \textquotedblleft{}make noise\textquotedblright{}). It lives on as Hindi \emph{bhaũrā} \textquotedblleft{}black bee\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9651).
\end{cousinweb}
